plan.reason: V4 has the highest risk score and concerns stateful single-pod cart storage. A pod kill directly tests restart behavior and whether persistent storage preserves cart contents. Customer-impact criteria distinguish temporary unavailability from silent data loss.

prediction.summary: Cart operations and checkout may briefly fail during restart; stored cart contents should remain intact after recovery because a persistent volume is configured.

plan.reason: Paymentservice is a single critical checkout dependency. A service outage directly tests whether checkout fails when payment is unavailable, without relying on target pod health as a criterion.

prediction.summary: Checkout attempts requiring payment should fail during the outage, producing materially elevated customer-visible errors compared with the 0.07% baseline error rate.

plan.reason: Checkout has high fan-in from six downstream services and is directly on the customer checkout path. Network delay tests latency propagation and distinguishes a latency-sensitive checkout bottleneck from a simple pod-availability failure.

prediction.summary: Checkout latency should increase substantially above the 34.7 ms mean and 59.95 ms baseline p95, with possible timeout-related customer errors even though the checkout pod remains running.

plan.reason: Frontend is the single site entrypoint. This test measures complete user-facing availability after a restart and complements the dependency outage and checkout latency tests with an entrypoint failure mode.

prediction.summary: Users should experience site errors or elevated latency while the sole frontend replica is being recreated; downstream services may remain healthy but inaccessible through the entrypoint.

replan_note: No prior experiments have been run, so rankings remain based on risk score, checkout-path criticality, and the ability to measure customer impact. The plan uses both pod_kill and pod_failure, plus network_delay, to distinguish state loss, dependency unavailability, latency propagation, and entrypoint availability. V4 includes the required integrity criterion because Redis cart state must be checked even with persistent storage configured.
